raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

`fast_pos_embed_interpolate` (patched into Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.5-MoE vision towers) converts every
bilinear interpolation index and weight to Python lists via `.tolist()` / `.extend()`, then rebuilds tensors from those
lists with `torch.tensor(...)` on every vision forward. For multi-image batches this is tens of thousands of Python
objects per forward.

This PR keeps the per-image tensors, concatenates them, and copies them to the target device once. The CPU arithmetic is
unchanged, so the output is bitwise identical to the previous implementation.

Related: #5572 and #5948 (both open) also touch `fast_pos_embed_interpolate` for device placement / refactoring, but keep the `.tolist()` round trip. This change is independent of them and easy to rebase onto either.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=fast_pos_embed_interpolate
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

New CPU test `tests/models/test_qwen_vl_pos_embed_interpolate_on_cpu.py` compares both patched functions
(`qwen3_vl`, `qwen3_5`) against the previous implementation with `torch.equal`, for FP32 and BF16 and for
single/multi-image, `t > 1`, and grids larger than `num_grid_per_side` (16 cases). Passes on transformers 5.5.3
(`verlai/verl:vllm024.dev1`) and 5.8.1 with torch 2.11.

Index/weight construction only (`hidden_size=1`, 8 CPU threads, median of 7):

| grid_thw | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 x [1, 32, 32] | 1.1 ms | 0.3 ms |
| 8 x [1, 46, 80] | 25.1 ms | 2.2 ms |
| 32 x [1, 46, 80] | 106.5 ms | 8.8 ms |

On GPU (1x A100-80GB, torch 2.11 + CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.8.1), with a random-weight Qwen3-VL vision tower at
Qwen3-VL-8B sizes (depth 27, hidden 1152, bf16, SDPA, `no_grad`). The output of both patched functions and of the full
vision forward is bitwise identical to the previous implementation on CUDA. Old/new runs interleaved, median:

| grid_thw | `fast_pos_embed_interpolate` before | after | vision tower forward before | after | saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 x [1, 32, 32] | 1.3 ms | 0.6 ms | 37.1 ms | 36.3 ms | 0.7 ms (2.0%) |
| 8 x [1, 46, 80] | 24.8 ms | 3.9 ms | 361.4 ms | 347.5 ms | 13.9 ms (3.8%) |
| 32 x [1, 46, 80] | 98.3 ms | 14.1 ms | 1458.3 ms | 1378.6 ms | 79.8 ms (5.5%) |

The interpolation runs on the host before the vision blocks are launched, so the GPU idles while it runs and the
saved host time shows up almost one-to-one in the forward latency.

### API and Usage Example

No API or config change.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/models/transformers/qwen3_vl.py`, `verl/models/transformers/qwen3_5.py`: append per-image index/weight tensors
  instead of extending Python lists; build `idx_tensor` / `weight_tensor` with `torch.stack(torch.cat(...))` followed by a
  single `.to(device, dtype)`. Interpolation math, the sequential BF16 summation order, and the merge permutation are
  untouched.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks (ruff 0.12.2 check/format, license check pass on changed files).
- [x] Add / Update the documentation. (N/A: no user-facing change)
- [x] Add unit test(s) to the CI workflow: `*_on_cpu.py`, picked up by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`.
- [x] Request CI in the `ci-request` channel.

+# limitations under the License.
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+
+def _reference_fast_pos_embed_interpolate(self, grid_thw):
+    """Previous implementation that round-trips indices and weights through Python lists."""
+    grid_thw_list = grid_thw.tolist()
+    grid_ts = [row[0] for row in grid_thw_list]
+    grid_hs = [row[1] for row in grid_thw_list]
+    grid_ws = [row[2] for row in grid_thw_list]
+    device = grid_thw.device
+
+    idx_list = [[] for _ in range(4)]
+    weight_list = [[] for _ in range(4)]
+
+    for t, h, w in grid_thw_list:
+        h_idxs = torch.linspace(0, self.num_grid_per_side - 1, h)
+        w_idxs = torch.linspace(0, self.num_grid_per_side - 1, w)
+
+        h_idxs_floor = h_idxs.int()
+        w_idxs_floor = w_idxs.int()
+        h_idxs_ceil = (h_idxs.int() + 1).clip(max=self.num_grid_per_side - 1)
+        w_idxs_ceil = (w_idxs.int() + 1).clip(max=self.num_grid_per_side - 1)
+
+        dh = h_idxs - h_idxs_floor
+        dw = w_idxs - w_idxs_floor
+
+        base_h = h_idxs_floor * self.num_grid_per_side
+        base_h_ceil = h_idxs_ceil * self.num_grid_per_side
+
+        indices = [
+            (base_h[None].T + w_idxs_floor[None]).flatten(),
+            (base_h[None].T + w_idxs_ceil[None]).flatten(),
+            (base_h_ceil[None].T + w_idxs_floor[None]).flatten(),
+            (base_h_ceil[None].T + w_idxs_ceil[None]).flatten(),
+        ]
+
+        weights = [
+            ((1 - dh)[None].T * (1 - dw)[None]).flatten(),
+            ((1 - dh)[None].T * dw[None]).flatten(),
+            (dh[None].T * (1 - dw)[None]).flatten(),
+            (dh[None].T * dw[None]).flatten(),
+        ]
+
+        for i in range(4):
+            idx_list[i].extend(indices[i].tolist())
+            weight_list[i].extend(weights[i].tolist())
+
+    idx_tensor = torch.tensor(idx_list, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
+    weight_tensor = torch.tensor(weight_list, dtype=self.pos_embed.weight.dtype, device=device)
+    pos_embeds = self.pos_embed(idx_tensor).to(device) * weight_tensor[:, :, None]
+    patch_pos_embeds = pos_embeds[0] + pos_embeds[1] + pos_embeds[2] + pos_embeds[3]
+
+    patch_pos_embeds = patch_pos_embeds.split([h * w for h, w in zip(grid_hs, grid_ws, strict=False)])
+
+    patch_pos_embeds_permute = []
+    merge_size = self.config.spatial_merge_size
+    for pos_embed, t, h, w in zip(patch_pos_embeds, grid_ts, grid_hs, grid_ws, strict=False):
+        pos_embed = pos_embed.repeat(t, 1)
+        pos_embed = (
+            pos_embed.view(t, h // merge_size, merge_size, w // merge_size, merge_size, -1)
+            .permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4, 5)
+            .flatten(0, 4)
+        )
+        patch_pos_embeds_permute.append(pos_embed)
+    return torch.cat(patch_pos_embeds_permute)
+
+
+def _load_impl(module_name):
+    module = pytest.importorskip(f"verl.models.transformers.{module_name}")
+    return module.fast_pos_embed_interpolate
+
+
+def _make_vision_model(dtype, num_grid_per_side=48, hidden_size=32, spatial_merge_size=2):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    pos_embed = torch.nn.Embedding(num_grid_per_side * num_grid_per_side, hidden_size).to(dtype)
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        pos_embed=pos_embed,
+        num_grid_per_side=num_grid_per_side,
+        config=SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=spatial_merge_size),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("module_name", ["qwen3_vl", "qwen3_5"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "grid_thw",
+    [
+        [[1, 2, 2]],
+        [[1, 16, 16]],
+        [[2, 8, 12], [1, 32, 20], [1, 4, 4]],
+        [[1, 96, 64]],  # larger than num_grid_per_side
+    ],
+)
+def test_fast_pos_embed_interpolate_matches_reference(module_name, dtype, grid_thw):
+    impl = _load_impl(module_name)
+    model = _make_vision_model(dtype)
+    grid_thw = torch.tensor(grid_thw, dtype=torch.long)
+
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        expected = _reference_fast_pos_embed_interpolate(model, grid_thw)
+        actual = impl(model, grid_thw)
+
+    assert actual.dtype == expected.dtype
+    assert actual.device == expected.device
+    assert torch.equal(actual, expected)
